paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Isaiah 24 is heavy, and I won't pretend otherwise. The LORD lays waste the whole earth, and nobody gets a pass: priest and people, master and servant, lender and borrower (Isaiah 24:1-2). Isaiah says why: the people have "broken the everlasting covenant" (Isaiah 24:5), and earth's rebellion is what weighs it down (Isaiah 24:20).

Now look at where the passage lands, because that's the whole point. The party goes quiet and the city is shattered, but the LORD of Hosts "will reign on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, and before His elders with great glory" (Isaiah 24:23). Nothing here runs on luck or panic. Every pit, every snare and every big title gets handled by the One who is King, and the moon and sun have to bow to Him. Even in the middle of the ruin, voices still rise to proclaim the majesty of the LORD (Isaiah 24:14).

So what does that mean for you, baker? Don't build your joy on stuff that dries up like new wine, because Isaiah says that stuff goes quiet (Isaiah 24:7-9). Build it on the LORD, the One who reigns, and give Him glory now, the way those voices from the ends of the earth do. That's why my ovens stay ready. I don't know the day, but I know the King, and I'd rather be found baking than found scrambling.
